producer_report.summary: Added `athena check --attribution`: a records-only check (athena_gate::attribution::check_attribution) reading athena/records (local ref, else origin tracking ref) and main's first-parent graph, never trailers. Walks from the earliest intent's expected base (anchor, not judged); a commit is attributed when a landing names it as host_commit and the cited intent matches (tree, parent); pending within 15 minutes of a matching intent, then fails; otherwise unattributed (sha named). Also reports missing branch, no intent, bad records, base off main, diverged refs, and non-fast-forward records commits (new records_branch::resolve_tip/audit_history). CLI flag conflicts with --history/--pr-head, exits 2 on findings. Added non-blocking `attribution` CI job and a CHANGELOG entry.

checks_run.note: completed without error exit; output too large to inspect per-suite

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test with a properly landed squash (landing-intent plus landing whose host_commit is the commit, head tree equal to the commit's tree, expected base equal to its parent) passes the attribution check.
criteria_check.evidence: cargo test -p athena-gate attribution: a_properly_landed_squash_passes ok.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a main commit with no landing record and no matching intent makes the check fail, and the report names that commit's sha as unattributed.
criteria_check.evidence: an_unrecorded_commit_fails_and_is_named ok; asserts Unattributed finding with the commit sha in commit and detail.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a commit with a matching landing-intent and no landing passes when the check time is within 15 minutes of the intent's creation time, and fails after 15 minutes.
Run `cargo test`: a records-branch history containing a commit that is not a fast-forward of its predecessor is reported by the check.
criteria_check.evidence: a_records_commit_that_is_not_a_fast_forward_is_reported and diverged_local_and_tracking_refs_are_reported ok; records_branch audit/resolve tests ok.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo run -- check --help`: `--attribution` is listed, and combining it with --history or --pr-head is rejected.
criteria_check.evidence: binary test check_help_lists_attribution_and_it_conflicts_with_the_other_modes passes: help lists --attribution, both combinations exit 2 with 'cannot be used with'.

criteria_check.criterion: The check reads only athena/records records and main's first-parent graph; nothing parses commit-message trailers; commits before the first intent's expected base are not judged. Code has doc comments citing records-history.md sections 5.2, 6, 10 and D111.
criteria_check.evidence: attribution.rs module docs cite §5.2, §6, §10, D111; no trailer/message calls; test commits_before_the_first_intents_base_are_not_judged and a_trailer_does_not_attribute_a_commit pass. The base commit itself is also not judged (departure noted).

criteria_check.criterion: .github/workflows/ci.yml has a new attribution job beside the history job: continue-on-error true, runs only on push to main and schedule, uses full-history checkout, explicitly fetches athena/records (e.g. `git fetch origin athena/records:athena/records`) before running `athena check --attribution`, pins actions by SHA like existing jobs, and is not a required check. The command reads the branch from the local or remote-tracking ref that was fetched.
criteria_check.evidence: Read the added job: if schedule or push to refs/heads/main, continue-on-error true, fetch-depth 0, same checkout SHA pin, fetch step before check; resolve_tip reads local then tracking ref.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo clippy`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo test`: all clean and passing for the workspace.
criteria_check.evidence: clippy -D warnings and fmt --check clean; full cargo test --locked finished without error exit (output not inspected per suite).

open_issues: Departed from plan decision 5: the base commit is the anchor and not judged; judging it would fail every real run since the base predates any intent.
Non-fast-forward is defined as a records commit dropping or changing a file its first parent held (plus diverged local/tracking refs); the design doc gives no sharper definition.
The ci.yml job uses persist-credentials: true so the fetch of athena/records can authenticate; token is read-only.
Any matching intent makes an unlanded commit pending, even one already fulfilled by another landing.
Declared-intervention records are not used for attribution yet.
If athena/records does not yet exist on origin, the CI fetch step fails; job is non-blocking.
The ci.yml job could not be run locally.
Full test suite output was not inspected per suite; only the absence of an error exit.
mistakes: A leftover `let _ = old;` remains in a commits-before-base test (harmless).
First wrote the walk to judge the base commit, which made the properly-landed test fail; corrected to treat the base as an anchor.
learnings: Records live at landing-intents/<id>.json and landings/<id>.json on athena/records; LandingIntent::matches(tree, parent) is the shared match rule.
Landing records commits carry the PR head as a second parent, so audit must follow first parents only.
Bash policy forbids heredocs and grep; use Edit/Grep tools.
desires: Ability to read large saved tool output to confirm full-suite results.
